verdictSummary: The visible AI photo editor loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Luminar Neo earns its keep through editor polish, assets, algorithms, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a focused local AI photo editor editor with import, a small set of transformations, undo, and standards-based export.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whatYouLose: high-fidelity color, format, and export handling
whyPeopleStillPay: Luminar Neo: Creative users pay for speed, output fidelity, nondestructive editing, and years of edge-case work hidden behind direct manipulation.
ongoingBurden: Maintain file-format compatibility, GPU and canvas performance, undo history, export quality, and platform-specific rendering.

priorArt.name: Penpot
priorArt.desc: Open-source collaborative design and prototyping platform.

alternatives.name: Affinity
alternatives.desc: A powerful free desktop photo editor for adjustments, masks, effects, and compositing; no catalog and no marketplace of one-click extensions.

alternatives.name: darktable
alternatives.desc: A complete non-destructive darkroom with masks, effects, lens correction, and denoise; automation is technical rather than magical.

facts.install: Install the Windows executable, macOS disk image, Linux package, Flatpak, or AppImage
facts.engines: A local non-generative imaging pipeline; current releases can use ONNX models for subject masking, denoising, and image upscaling without a cloud account
facts.dataFormat: Original photos stay untouched; edits, ratings, tags, and history are stored in a local SQLite library and portable XMP sidecar files, with thumbnails and cache data in the user profile
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a complete technical darkroom, but does not provide Luminar's polished one-click generative erase, sky replacement, portrait AI, creative effects, and extension catalog.
facts.setupBlocker: macOS may require a Gatekeeper right-click Open or xattr step; the larger obstacle is learning darktable's module-heavy workflow rather than installation

alternatives.name: RapidRAW
alternatives.desc: Local RAW editing with AI masks, denoise, presets, blur, healing, and batch work; fewer canned sky-and-glow tricks, much less rent.

facts.install: Install the Windows .exe, macOS .dmg, or Linux AppImage/DEB/Flatpak; Android is an experimental sideload
facts.engines: Local subject, sky, and foreground masking, NIND denoising, LaMa inpainting, and optional handoff to a user-run ComfyUI backend
facts.dataFormat: Photos are never moved; non-destructive adjustments are stored in a documented .rrdata sidecar next to each image, while thumbnails, logs, and downloaded models live in local application data
facts.gapVsPaid: It includes useful local AI tools, but has far fewer finished one-click effects and creative assets and is much less mature than Luminar Neo.
facts.setupBlocker: Desktop binaries are unsigned, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper need manual bypass steps; Linux AppImage users may also need libfuse2

rejectedAlternatives.name: PhotoPrism
rejectedAlternatives.desc: An asset library with light editing is not a desktop effects editor, however often photo-server lists pretend otherwise.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Luminar Neo is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Luminar Neo, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + Canvas API.
Primary job: Build a focused local AI photo editor editor with import, a small set of transformations, undo, and standards-based export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: large template and asset libraries; color-management edge cases; cloud collaboration and mobile apps.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
